nodes.description: Procoagulant HK activity falls below 1%. HK is a multidomain cystatin superfamily protein; its light chain carries domain 5, which binds anionic surfaces and the endothelial receptor gC1qR in a zinc-dependent way, and domain 6, which binds prekallikrein and factor XI. Truncation removes both, so the protein that remains cannot act as a cofactor even where it is present.

nodes.description: Both KNG1 alleles carry a nonsense, frameshift or splice change producing a premature stop codon. The truncated product loses the C-terminal light chain, which is where both of HK's cofactor functions live.

genetic_context.description: Germline and biallelic, homozygous or compound heterozygous. zygosity is deliberately omitted rather than set to HOMOZYGOUS, because ZygosityEnum offers no biallelic value and either specific value would be wrong for some of the reported patients. Every reported deficiency-causing allele is truncating; the single reported missense allele of this gene causes a different disease.

nodes.description: A secondary reduction in plasma prekallikrein, because prekallikrein circulates bound to HK and is not retained without it. It is a consequence of the deficiency, not a second disorder, and is one half of the pattern that leads to misdiagnosis.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with HK deficiency appeared asymptomatic and had decreased levels of prekallikrein and factor XI, which could lead to misdiagnosis.

nodes.description: The reciprocal activation of factor XII and prekallikrein on a surface, and the onward activation of factor XI, cannot proceed efficiently. This is what the activated partial thromboplastin time measures, so the assay is markedly prolonged. It corrects on 1:1 mixing with normal plasma, because the missing component is a factor and not an inhibitor, which is the step that separates this from an acquired inhibitor.

nodes.description: Without HK, prekallikrein and factor XI are not carried to the activating surface. The physiological assembly runs through gC1qR, which clusters factor XII and HK into a higher-order ternary complex and so acts as a chaperone bringing the contact factors together; that clustering is the prelude to both bradykinin generation and intrinsic-pathway coagulation. With no HK there is no such complex.

evidence.reference_title: Factor XII and kininogen asymmetric assembly with gC1qR/C1QBP/P32 is governed by allostery.
evidence.snippet: These results support the conclusion that extracellular gC1qR can act as a chaperone to cluster contact factors, which may be a prelude for initiating the cascades that drive bradykinin generation and the intrinsic pathway of coagulation.

nodes.description: A markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time with a normal prothrombin time, present from birth and correcting on 1:1 mixing with normal plasma. It is essentially the whole of the disease's presentation: in every reported case the deficiency was found during the work-up of an unexplained long aPTT rather than because of a symptom.

nodes.description: The HK-null mouse, used here in Plasmodium berghei ANKA experimental cerebral malaria. It is the model behind this entry's statement that losing HK is protective rather than harmful: Kng1-/- mice were significantly protected from neurologic deterioration and brain edema compared with wild-type, alongside bradykinin receptor knockouts, which is what places the protection on the bradykinin arm.
nodes.id: Kng1-null mouse in experimental cerebral malaria

evidence.reference_title: Bradykinin contributes to vasogenic edema in murine experimental cerebral malaria.
evidence.snippet: HK-null (Kng1-/-), combined BK B1- and B2 receptor-null (Bdkrb1-/-Bdkrb2-/-), BK B2 receptor-null (Bdkrb2-/-), or BK B1 receptor-null (Bdkrb1-/-) mice were protected significantly from neurologic deterioration and brain edema compared with wild-type mice.

nodes.description: Physiological clotting is driven by tissue factor and factor VIIa with thrombin feedback, not by contact activation, so the loss of the contact arm leaves haemostasis intact. This node exists to carry an explicitly negative finding: affected people do not bleed, and the absence of a bleeding phenotype is the clinically important fact about this disease rather than a gap in its curation.

nodes.description: The other arm of the contact system. Plasma kallikrein cleaves HK to release bradykinin, which acts on endothelial B1 and B2 receptors to produce vasodilation, increased vascular permeability and oedema. Without HK there is no substrate, so this arm is blunted. In mouse models that loss is protective rather than harmful, which is the observation behind the idea that the contact system is a safe antithrombotic drug target. No human phenotype is attributed to it here.

nodes.description: Prekallikrein and factor XI circulate bound to HK. With no HK to carry them they are present at reduced plasma levels, which is a consequence of this disease rather than a second coagulation defect. The systematic review names this as the specific route to misdiagnosis, because a panel showing low prekallikrein and low factor XI next to a long aPTT reads like a different disorder.

nodes.description: A nonsense variant found homozygous in a large Chinese family. The 67-year-old propositus was asymptomatic and came to attention only through an isolated prolonged aPTT; his procoagulant HK activity was under 1%, and prekallikrein activity was reduced in him and in two affected sisters.

evidence.snippet: This Chinese family has a novel KGN1 nonsense variant, C to T, at nucleotide position 1456 leading to a stop codon in position 486 (p. Gln486*).

nodes.description: A two-base insertion in exon 4 producing a frameshift and a premature stop at residue 183. The homozygous proband had 0.9% HK activity; his three heterozygous children had partially reduced activity.

evidence.reference_title: A novel frameshift mutation in exon 4 causing a deficiency of high-molecular-weight kininogen in a patient with splenic infarction.
evidence.snippet: Direct sequencing of his HMWK gene showed a homozygous "TC" insertion at c523-524 in exon 4. This insertion led to an amino acid substitution, Ser175Ser, resulting in a frameshift mutation and a premature stop codon in amino acid 183.
